what: The heuristic precomputes CVRP problem structure in LlmHeuristic::new(). It parses propositional fact names to identify depot, customers, current-location facts, and visited facts. It builds a distance matrix from grounded operator costs: 'visit' gives direct customer-to-customer or depot-to-customer costs, 'return-to-depot' gives customer-to-depot costs, and 'visit-via-depot' gives via-depot route-switch costs. Missing direct distances are completed symmetrically where possible. It also attempts exact-name numeric lookups for load(), vehicles(), capacity(), max_vehicles(), and demand(c_i); if capacity/demand/max_vehicles are missing it degrades permissively (f64::MAX for capacity/max_vehicles, 0.0 for demands). For each node it sorts candidate customers by greedy insertion cost dist[from][c]+dist[c][depot]. At evaluation time, it reads the numeric fluents and propositional state to determine current location, visited customers, load, and vehicles. It then greedily constructs remaining routes from the current state: it continues the current route while capacity allows, selecting the first feasible unvisited customer in insertion-cost order; when no customer fits but a new vehicle is allowed, it switches via depot using the precomputed via-depot cost; otherwise it falls back with a strong penalty. The returned estimate is the sum of direct, via-depot, and final return-to-depot costs for the greedy completion.
why: The CVRP state is best summarized by current location, current load, vehicles used, unvisited customers, and remaining route cost. Greedy nearest-insertion-style route construction is fast, non-admissible, and produces a realistic upper bound on the remaining routing cost without solving a full VRP at every state. Precomputing distances from operator costs avoids fragile parsing of derived travel-cost variables. Sorted insertion-cost neighbor lists make evaluation cheap, which matters because compute_heuristic is called many times. Capacity and vehicle limits are respected when those numeric values are available, and permissive defaults keep the heuristic robust across translator variants where capacity/demand/max_vehicles are folded into derived expressions.
